statement.p: Calculate the derivative using the appropriate rule or combination of rules. f(x)=\frac{e^{x}}{\left(e^{x}+3\right)\mathopen{}\left(x+3\right)}

static.solution: f'(x) we begin with quotient rule f'(x)= \frac{(e^x+3)(x+3)\frac{d}{dx}[e^x]-e^x\frac{d}{dx}[(e^x+3)(x+3)]}{((e^x+3)(x+3))^2}. Next, recall that \frac{d}{dx}[e^x]=e^x, and use the product rule to compute \frac{d}{dx}[(e^x+3)(x+3)]=\frac{d}{dx}[e^x+3](x+3)+(e^x+3)\frac{d}{dx}[x+3] which is (e^x)(x+3)+(e^x+3)(1). Therefore f'(x)= \frac{(e^x+3)(x+3)\cdot e^x-e^x\cdot (e^x(x+3)+(e^x+3))}{((e^x+3)(x+3))^2} and after factoring out e^x in the numerator, expanding (e^x+3)(x+3)=xe^x+3\cdot e^x+3 x+3\cdot 3, and distributing the minus sign, we get f'(x)=\frac{e^x(xe^x+3 x+3 e^x - xe^x-3 e^x-e^x-3)}{((e^x+3)(x+3))^2} which simplifies to f'(x)=\frac{e^x(3 x - e^x-3)}{((e^x+3)(x+3))^2}.
